usage: to leave it to an accountant
examples: It's easier to leave the year-end tax settlement to an accountant.
The CPA exam is really hard to pass.
회사에 회계사가 한 명 있어서 든든해요.
We have an accountant at the company, so it's reassuring.
nuance: 회계사 means a certified public accountant who handles a company's books, audits, and taxes, and it carries the prestige of a hard licensing exam. For a tax-specialist you visit at filing time, Koreans more often say 세무사 instead.
mistakes: Saying 회계사이에요 instead of correct 회계사예요
Confusing 회계사 the person with 회계 the accounting itself

usage: to leave it to a tax accountant
examples: Since I'm self-employed, I leave the tax filing to a tax accountant.
I met a tax accountant before filing my income tax.
A tax accountant's fee is cheaper than I thought.
nuance: 세무사 means a licensed tax specialist who files returns and advises on taxes, the person freelancers and small-business owners hire every spring. Unlike 회계사, who covers broad accounting and audits, the 세무사 focuses specifically on taxes.
mistakes: Confusing 세무사 the tax advisor with 회계사 the broader accountant
Saying 세금사, which is not a real word; the correct term is 세무사

examples: I'm a developer working at a startup.
Developer salaries have gone up a lot lately.
I'm studying coding to switch jobs to a developer role.
nuance: 개발자 is the everyday Korean word for a software developer and is far more common in tech workplaces than the older 프로그래머. People specify the field, like 앱 개발자, 웹 개발자, or 백엔드 개발자.
mistakes: Saying 개발자이에요 instead of correct 개발자예요
Confusing 개발자 the person with 개발 the development work

examples: I quit my company and now work as a freelancer.
프리랜서는 일정을 자유롭게 정할 수 있어요.
Freelancers can set their schedule freely.
Since I'm a freelancer, my income differs every month.
nuance: 프리랜서 is the borrowed word for someone who works independently for various clients instead of one employer, very common among designers, writers, and translators. It often pairs with the upside of freedom and the downside of unstable income.
mistakes: Saying 프리랜서이에요 instead of correct 프리랜서예요
Spelling it 프리랜셔; the standard form is 프리랜서

usage: to live as a self-employed person
examples: I'm a small-business owner running a little café.
Self-employed owners are heavily affected by the economy.
There are really a lot of self-employed people in Korea.
nuance: 자영업자 means someone who runs their own small business, like a café, shop, or restaurant, rather than working for a company. It is a big social group in Korea and often appears in news about the economy and small-business hardship.
mistakes: Saying 자영업자이에요 instead of correct 자영업자예요
Confusing 자영업자 the owner with 자영업 the self-employment itself

usage: to work as a delivery rider
examples: 배달원이 음식을 문 앞에 놓고 갔어요.
The delivery worker left the food at the door.
놓고 가다 means leave and go
비 오는 날엔 배달원이 정말 고생해요.
On rainy days delivery riders really have a hard time.
Many people do delivery work as a side gig these days.
nuance: 배달원 means a person who delivers food or packages, usually by motorcycle, and it is a very visible job in Korea's huge delivery culture. In casual speech people also say 배달 기사님 or just 라이더 for app-based riders.
mistakes: Confusing 배달원 the person with 배달 the delivery service
Calling them 배달부, which sounds dated; 배달원 or 배달 기사님 is natural now

usage: a sales rep comes to visit
examples: I'm a salesperson at a cosmetics company.
For a salesperson, performance numbers really matter.
Thanks to a kind sales rep, I bought a car.
nuance: 영업사원 means a company salesperson who meets customers and sells products, judged largely by their 실적, or sales numbers. The shorter 영업직 refers to the sales position or field in general, while 영업사원 is the individual person.
mistakes: Saying 영업사원예요 instead of correct 영업사원이에요
Confusing 영업사원 the person with 영업 the sales activity

examples: I'm an English instructor who teaches at an academy.
헬스장 강사가 운동 자세를 고쳐 줬어요.
The gym instructor corrected my exercise posture.
It's been three years working as a yoga instructor.
ㄴ 지 됐다 means it's been since
nuance: 강사 means an instructor or lecturer who teaches at a private academy, gym, or culture center, distinct from 선생님 used for a schoolteacher. You usually name the subject, like 영어 강사, 요가 강사, or 헬스 강사.
mistakes: Saying 강사이에요 instead of correct 강사예요
Confusing 강사 the academy instructor with 교수 the university professor

examples: 힘들 때 상담사와 이야기하면 도움이 돼요.
Talking with a counselor when things are hard helps.
I'm a counselor working at a school.
nuance: 상담사 means a professional who gives advice or counseling, from mental-health counselors to career or call-center advisors, depending on the field named in front. For a licensed mental-health specialist, the fuller term 상담 심리사 is also used.
mistakes: Saying 상담사이에요 instead of correct 상담사예요
Confusing 상담사 the counselor with 상담 the consultation session

examples: 집 구할 때 공인중개사한테 도움을 받았어요.
I got help from a licensed agent when finding a place.
집을 구하다 means find a home
We did the contract at the real estate office.
요즘 공인중개사 시험 준비하는 사람이 많아요.
Many people are preparing for the agent license exam now.
nuance: 공인중개사 is the licensed real estate agent who arranges 전세, 월세, and home sales, and you will deal with one whenever you rent in Korea. People casually call the office 부동산, so 부동산 가다 means going to the agent's office.
mistakes: Calling the person 부동산; 부동산 is the office or property, the person is 공인중개사
Dropping the 공인 and saying just 중개사 in formal contexts

examples: I got a headache medicine recommended by the pharmacist.
약사가 약 먹는 방법을 알려 줬어요.
The pharmacist told me how to take the medicine.
My older sister is a pharmacist working at a pharmacy.
nuance: 약사 means a licensed pharmacist who dispenses medicine and advises on dosage at a 약국. In Korea pharmacists actively recommend over-the-counter medicine, so asking the 약사 directly is a normal first step for minor symptoms.
mistakes: Saying 약사이에요 instead of correct 약사예요
Confusing 약사 the pharmacist with 의사 the doctor

usage: to work as a social worker
examples: I'm a social worker at a welfare center.
The social worker helps the elderly.
I'm studying to get the social worker license.
자격증을 따다 means get a license
nuance: 사회복지사 means a social worker who supports vulnerable people such as the elderly, children, or low-income families, usually at a 복지관 or public office. It is a licensed job, so people talk about earning the 자격증 to enter the field.
mistakes: Saying 사회복지사이에요 instead of correct 사회복지사예요
Shortening it to 복지사 in formal contexts; the full term is 사회복지사
